name: International Junior Science Olympiad (IJSO)
description: An annual science olympiad for students under sixteen, combining theory and practical tests across biology, chemistry and physics. Around 50 member countries send national delegations, selected through their own junior science olympiad.
prize: Individual gold, silver and bronze medals plus team awards.

stages.name: National Standard Examination in Junior Science (NSEJS)

name: International Biology Olympiad (IBO)
organizer: IBO Coordinating Centre and the annual host country
description: An annual biology competition for secondary school students, combining a written theory exam with hands on laboratory practicals. Each country sends a national team of up to four students selected through its own biology olympiad.
prize: Gold, silver or bronze medal awarded by score.

name: International Brain Bee
description: A three-tiered neuroscience quiz competition for teens. Students who win their country's National Brain Bee go on to represent that country at the International Brain Bee World Championship.
prize: Advancement to the IBB World Championship; national champions represent their country.

name: International Chemistry Olympiad (IChO)
organizer: IChO International Steering Committee and the annual host country
description: A theoretical and experimental chemistry competition for secondary school students, held annually since 1968. National teams of up to four students qualify through their own country's chemistry olympiad.
prize: Gold, silver or bronze medal awarded by score.

name: International Physics Olympiad (IPhO)
organizer: IPhO Secretariat and the annual host country
description: A theoretical and experimental physics competition for secondary school students who have not yet started university. National teams of up to five students, plus two team leaders, qualify through their own country's physics olympiad.
prize: Gold, silver or bronze medal awarded by score.

name: International Olympiad on Astronomy and Astrophysics (IOAA)
description: An annual astronomy and astrophysics competition for high school students, with theoretical, data analysis and observational rounds. National teams are selected through each country's own astronomy olympiad.
prize: Gold, silver and bronze medals plus honourable mentions.

name: Regeneron International Science and Engineering Fair (ISEF)
description: The largest pre-college science and engineering fair in the world. Students present an original research project after winning a place at a Society-affiliated regional, state or national fair.
prize: USD 100,000 George D. Yancopoulos Innovator Award, plus category and special awards.

name: Science Olympiad
description: A US team tournament spanning roughly 23 lab, study and build events each season. Teams advance from regional to state tournaments and then to the National Tournament.
prize: National Tournament championship title and individual event medals.

name: World Robot Olympiad (WRO)
description: A global robotics competition for teams of two or three students, ages 8 to 19 (up to 22 in the Future Engineers category), plus a coach. Teams design, build and program a robot for the season's theme and qualify through their own country's national event.
prize: International Final trophies and category awards; exact amounts vary by season and country.

name: International Earth Science Olympiad (IESO)
description: An annual competition for secondary students that tests earth science knowledge through written exams, a team Earth System Project and field investigations. National teams qualify through their own country's earth science olympiad selection process.
prize: Gold, silver and bronze medals by individual score, plus a team project award.

dates.label: IESO 2027 (host to be confirmed, following the usual August pattern)

name: International Olympiad in Artificial Intelligence (IOAI)
organizer: IOAI Foundation and the annual host institution
description: A science olympiad for high school students covering machine learning, natural language processing and AI safety through both theory and hands on coding rounds. National teams are selected through each country's own AI olympiad process.
prize: Gold, silver or bronze medal awarded by score.

name: European Physics Olympiad (EuPhO)
organizer: EuPhO organizing committee and the annual host country
description: An annual theoretical physics competition open to secondary school students from Europe and invited guest countries. Each delegation sends a team, and problems are set at a level comparable to the International Physics Olympiad.
prize: Gold, silver and bronze medals plus honourable mentions.

dates.label: EuPhO 2027 (host to be confirmed, following the usual mid-June pattern)

name: International BioGENEius Challenge
description: A biotechnology research competition for high school age students, judged across Global Healthcare, Global Sustainability and Global Environment tracks. Finalists advance from state and regional BioGENEius competitions to present their research before a panel of industry and academic judges.
prize: Cash awards and recognition across three research tracks at the national final.

dates.label: National final (following the usual autumn pattern, exact 2027 dates not yet posted)

name: National Science Bowl (NSB)
description: A fast-paced, buzzer led team science quiz run by the U.S. Department of Energy across divisions from middle school to the collegiate level. Regional tournaments feed into an all expenses paid National Finals in Washington DC.
prize: Trophies, scholarships and prizes at the National Finals.

name: ExploraVision
organizer: National Science Teaching Association and Toshiba
description: A team competition asking students in grades K-12 to imagine the future of a current technology and research its likely evolution over the next twenty years. Teams submit a paper, web page and graphic presentation, and regional winners build physical prototypes for the national phase.
prize: Regional winners receive savings bonds; national winners get a trip and up to USD 10,000 in savings bonds.

name: American Rocketry Challenge
organizer: American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics (AIA) and the National Association of Rocketry
description: Teams of US students in grades 6-12 design, build, and fly a model rocket carrying two raw eggs to a target altitude and flight duration, scored on how close each qualification flight comes to the targets. The top 100 teams earn a place at the National Finals in Northern Virginia, which distributes 100,000 dollars in awards.
prize: A share of 100,000 dollars in awards at the National Finals; the winning team represents the US at the International Rocketry Challenge.

name: AGU Bright STaRS
description: Middle and high school students present original Earth and space science research as posters in the Bright STaRS session at AGU's Annual Meeting each December, with feedback from attending scientists. Participation is arranged through a student's research program or school supervisor, who submits the abstract.
prize: Presentation at the AGU Annual Meeting with complimentary conference registration; no cash prize.

dates.label: Bright STaRS poster session at the AGU Annual Meeting

name: AAPT High School Physics Photo Contest
description: Students submit a photograph that captures a physics principle in everyday life together with a short essay explaining the science, judged in separate natural and contrived photo categories. Schools may enter up to 15 photos each year.
prize: Cash prizes and AAPT recognition for winning photos in each category.

name: National Young Astronomer Award (NYAA)
description: A national award recognizing original astronomical research or observing programs by US students aged 14 to 19, judged by a panel of professional astronomers. Winners are honored at the League's ALCon national convention.
prize: Telescope and expense-paid trip to ALCon for the first-place winner.

name: USA Biolympiad (USABO)
description: A national biology exam series for US high school students that narrows from an online Open Exam through a Semifinal Exam to National Finalists who compete in person at Harvard University. The top scorers there form the four-student team that represents the US at the International Biology Olympiad.
prize: Advancement to National Finals at Harvard University; top scorers earn a place on the four-student US team for the International Biology Olympiad.

dates.label: National Finals (Harvard University, following the usual spring pattern)

name: Australian Biology Olympiad (ABO)
description: The national biology exam of the Australian Science Olympiads program, sat by students at their own school before top performers are invited to a residential Summer School at the Australian National University. Established in 1992, its strongest performers go on to trial for the Australian team at the International Biology Olympiad.
prize: Selection for the ANU Summer School and a chance to trial for Australia's International Biology Olympiad team.

dates.label: 2027 Biology Olympiad exam (following the usual late-July pattern)

name: Singapore Biology Olympiad (SBO)
organizer: Singapore Institute of Biology (SIBiol) and Ministry of Education
description: An annual biology exam for junior college students in Singapore, run since 2000 through a theory paper followed by a practical test for shortlisted candidates. Top performers receive medals and may enter further training for Singapore's International Biology Olympiad team.
prize: Gold, silver and bronze medals; top performers are considered for Singapore's IBO training squad.

name: British Biology Olympiad (BBO)
description: A two-paper multiple-choice biology exam open to final-year pre-university students across the UK, run through the UK Biology Competitions programme. Gold, silver and bronze certificates are awarded by score, and top performers are invited to UK team selection for the International Biology Olympiad.
prize: Gold, silver, bronze, highly commended and commended e-certificates; top scorers are invited to UK team selection for the IBO.

dates.label: British Biology Olympiad exam window opens
British Biology Olympiad exam window closes

name: New Zealand International Biology Olympiad (NZIBO)
organizer: New Zealand International Biology Olympiad Trust
description: A three-stage programme for New Zealand secondary students that starts with a National Entrance Exam, continues through online tutorials for the top scorers, and ends with a practical training and selection camp. Graduates of the programme form New Zealand's team at the International Biology Olympiad.
prize: Advancement through the tutorial and camp stages toward a place on New Zealand's IBO team; NZIBO scholarships are available toward programme fees.

dates.label: Selection exam for Practical Training Camp

name: Canadian Biology Olympiad (CBO)
description: A national online exam for Canadian secondary school students that combines theoretical and practical-style questions in the manner of the International Biology Olympiad. Top scorers attend a training camp at UBC Okanagan, and the strongest performers there are selected for Canada's IBO team.
prize: Invitation to the national training camp at UBC Okanagan; top performers represent Canada at the IBO.

dates.label: CBO 2027 competition (following the usual April pattern)

name: National Biology Competition
description: A 50-question multiple-choice exam run by the University of Toronto that lets grade 9-12 students anywhere test their biology knowledge against a Canadian and international field. Schools with at least five entrants receive team rankings, and top individual scorers and schools earn certificates and monetary awards.
prize: Certificates and monetary awards for top scorers; Certificates of Excellence for the top three Canadian and top three international schools.

dates.label: 2027 exam window (following the usual April pattern)

name: Genes in Space
organizer: miniPCR bio, Boeing, New England Biolabs and the ISS National Laboratory
description: A US contest that asks students in grades 7 through 12 to design a DNA experiment that solves a real problem in space exploration, with no prior lab experience required. The winning team's experiment is carried out in orbit by astronauts aboard the International Space Station using miniPCR biotechnology.
prize: The winning experiment is flown to and run on the International Space Station; finalists' schools receive a DNA Discovery System valued at USD 950.

dates.label: Winning 2026 experiment launches to the ISS (following the announced 2027 launch window)

name: Indian National Biology Olympiad (INBO)
organizer: Homi Bhabha Centre for Science Education (HBCSE) and Indian Association of Physics Teachers (IAPT)
description: The second of three stages India uses to select its International Biology Olympiad team, open to students who clear the National Standard Examination in Biology. Roughly 300 students who pass INBO are narrowed further at an Orientation cum Selection Camp at HBCSE Mumbai to choose the four-student national team.
prize: Advancement to the Orientation cum Selection Camp; selection for India's four-student IBO team.

name: National Biology Bee
description: A buzzer-based quiz tournament for US students split into Junior Varsity (grades 9-10) and Varsity (grades 11-12) divisions. Students must first pass a National Qualifying Exam before advancing to the National Championships, an online tournament of preliminary and playoff rounds.
prize: Champion titles in the Varsity and Junior Varsity divisions and national recognition through IAC.

name: U.S. National Chemistry Olympiad (USNCO)
description: A three-round US chemistry competition run through local ACS sections, moving from a Local Exam to a National Exam and finally a Study Camp for the top scorers. The four highest-performing Study Camp students form the US team for the International Chemistry Olympiad.
prize: Advancement to the national Study Camp; selection for the four-student US team at IChO.

dates.label: Local Exam window (following the usual late-February to March pattern)
National Exam window (following the usual mid-April pattern)
Study Camp (following the usual early-June pattern)

name: UK Chemistry Olympiad (UKChO)
description: The Royal Society of Chemistry's flagship exam for post-16 students, opening with a two-hour written Round One paper sat at more than a thousand schools. Top scorers advance to a residential Round Two at the University of Nottingham, from which the four-student UK team for the International Chemistry Olympiad is chosen.
prize: Gold, silver and bronze certificates by score band; Round Two finalists compete for a place on the UK's IChO team.

dates.label: Round One exam (2027, following the usual late-January pattern)

name: Schools' Analyst Competition
description: A practical analytical chemistry competition run by the Royal Society of Chemistry's Analytical Division for teams of three Year 12 (or equivalent) students in the UK and Ireland. Teams receive a kit of forensic or cosmetic science themed challenges, from titrations to chromatographic separations, to complete at their own school.
prize: Certificates for winning teams; regional winners receive additional prizes and advance toward UK-wide recognition.

dates.label: Competition kits delivered and event window opens
Schools' Analyst Competition 2027 (following the usual spring pattern)

name: Canadian Chemistry Olympiad (CCO)
description: A training and exam programme for Canadian high school students with advanced chemistry interest, built around monthly problem sets and a take-home exam each March. Top performers are invited to a residential training camp, from which Canada's four-student team for the International Chemistry Olympiad is chosen.
prize: Invitation to the national training camp; selection for Canada's four-student IChO team.

dates.label: Take-home exam (following the usual March pattern)

name: Canadian Chemistry Contest (CCC)
description: An in-school multiple-choice and short-essay chemistry exam aimed at Canada's top chemistry students, roughly the top ten percent of secondary and CEGEP students under 20. It is written under teacher supervision and, unlike the Canadian Chemistry Olympiad, does not lead to international team selection, serving instead as a broader annual benchmark of chemistry achievement.
prize: Certificates and national ranking recognition from the Chemical Institute of Canada.

name: Australian Chemistry Olympiad Program (ACOP)
description: The chemistry stream of the Australian Science Olympiads, sat by students at their own school before top performers attend a residential Summer School at the Australian National University. Strong performers there go on to trial for the Australian team at the International Chemistry Olympiad.
prize: Selection for the ANU Summer School and a chance to trial for Australia's IChO team.

dates.label: 2027 Chemistry Olympiad exam (following the usual late-July pattern)

name: You Be The Chemist Challenge
description: A free team competition for US students in grades 5 through 8 that pairs timed chemistry knowledge questions with a video challenge pitching a sustainability-focused start-up idea. Teams advance from Regional Challenges through State Challenges to a National Challenge in Houston, Texas.
prize: Scholarship awards for top teams at the National Challenge in Houston, Texas.

dates.label: Regional Challenges (following the usual winter pattern)
National Challenge (Houston, TX, following the usual spring pattern)

name: New Zealand Chemistry Olympiad (NZChO)
description: An in-school chemistry assessment run by a volunteer committee of New Zealand secondary and tertiary teachers, open to any Year 12 student or below. Results are used to invite a training group of top scorers, who study extension modules over summer ahead of team selection for the International Chemistry Olympiad.
prize: Invitation to the NZChO training group; registration fees are donated to education charities.

dates.label: 2027 exam window (following the usual September pattern)

name: Singapore Junior Chemistry Olympiad (SJChO)
description: An annual two-round chemistry competition for upper secondary students in Singapore, drawing more than 2,000 entrants from over 80 schools each year. It complements the senior Singapore Chemistry Olympiad by giving younger students an early taste of olympiad-style chemistry problem solving.
prize: Medals and certificates by score band; strong performers are encouraged toward the senior Singapore Chemistry Olympiad.

name: Indian National Chemistry Olympiad (INChO)
organizer: Homi Bhabha Centre for Science Education (HBCSE) and Indian Association of Physics Teachers (IAPT)
description: The second of three stages India uses to select its International Chemistry Olympiad team, open to students who clear the National Standard Examination in Chemistry. Roughly 300 qualifiers sit INChO, and the strongest performers are invited to an Orientation cum Selection Camp at HBCSE Mumbai to choose the four-student national team.
prize: Advancement to the Orientation cum Selection Camp; selection for India's four-student IChO team.

name: Chemistry Olympiad Ireland
organizer: Institute of Chemistry of Ireland and Irish Science Teachers' Association
description: A two-round chemistry exam open to final-year secondary students across Ireland and Northern Ireland, with Round One sat at assessment centres including DCU, UCC, QUB and TUS. Top scorers from Round One advance to an in-person Round Two at Dublin City University, from which Ireland's team for the International Chemistry Olympiad is chosen.
prize: Advancement to Round Two at Dublin City University; selection for Ireland's IChO team.

dates.label: Round 1 (DCU, UCC, QUB and TUS assessment centres)
Chemistry Olympiad Ireland 2027 Round 1 (following the usual February pattern)

name: National Ocean Sciences Bowl (NOSB)
description: A quiz bowl for teams of four or five US high schoolers covering ocean biology, chemistry, geology, physics and policy through lockout-buzzer and team-challenge rounds. About 25 regional bowls each year qualify teams for the National Finals, with a scored virtual poster round piloted alongside the buzzer competition in 2027.
prize: Regional bowl trophies; National Finals recognition and scholarships for top teams.

dates.label: National Finals (following the usual spring pattern)

name: MATE ROV Competition
organizer: Marine Advanced Technology Education (MATE) Center and Marine Technology Society
description: An underwater robotics competition in which student teams design, build and pilot a remotely operated vehicle through marine-workplace missions, then present an engineering notebook, poster and oral presentation to judges. Teams progress through the SCOUT, NAVIGATOR and RANGER classes at regional events toward the international World Championship.
prize: Class awards and technical achievement prizes at regional events; qualification to the World Championship.

dates.label: Northern Gulf Coast regional (Dauphin Island Sea Lab)

name: SeaPerch Challenge
organizer: RoboNation, sponsored by the Office of Naval Research
description: A program in which elementary, middle and high school teams build an underwater remotely operated vehicle from a SeaPerch kit and compete in local and regional challenges built around a yearly marine engineering theme. Teams that place well regionally earn an invitation to the International SeaPerch Challenge.
prize: Regional challenge awards; qualification to the International SeaPerch Challenge.

dates.label: International SeaPerch Challenge 2027 (following the usual late-May pattern)

name: Marine Science Scholarship Competition
organizer: American Salvage Association and North American Marine Environment Protection Association
description: A research paper competition open to US high school and undergraduate students who have entered a science or engineering fair project in a marine-related field such as marine environmental care, ocean engineering or underwater robotics. A technical committee of maritime professionals reviews a project abstract and paper, and winners present their work at NAMEPA's Annual Conference in New York.
prize: USD 500 first place, USD 250 second place and USD 100 third place, plus sponsored travel to NAMEPA's Annual Conference in New York.

dates.label: Awards presented at NAMEPA Annual Conference (New York)
